region.text: the district and city of Trier

ledger.note: 898: Archbishop Radbod of Trier receives complete immunity and imperial immediacy. 'In 898, Archbishop Radbod received complete immunity from all taxes for the entire episcopal territory'; infobox 'imperial immediacy 898'; just after the 900 murder of Zwentibold the district and city of Trier were granted to him outright. The page gives no boundary.
1018: Emperor Henry II gives Koblenz to the Archbishop of Trier. 'In 1018, the city was given by the emperor Henry II to the archbishop-elector of Trier after receiving a charter.'

region.text: Boppard and its outlying lands, pledged to Baldwin in 1309 and 1312

ledger.note: 1309: Emperor Henry VII pledges Boppard to Archbishop Baldwin. 'Until 1309, Boppard was a free imperial city'; 'In 1309 and 1312, Emperor Heinrich VII pledged Boppard' to his brother Baldwin with its outlying lands; Baldwin later had the town 'stormed and quelled' after its 1327 council (undated); in 1368 Charles IV promised the pledge would not be redeemed. Reviewer eu-09-g: counterpart was holy-roman-empire, whose dossier ends in 1259 (successor holy-roman-empire-minor-states).

region.text: the territory 'along the river Moselle between Trier, near the French border, and Koblenz on the Rhine' (Electorate of Trier page): the Moselle valley within 22 km of the river, Trier and Koblenz within 30 km, inside Rhineland-Palatinate

ledger.note: 1333: the Moselle territory between Trier and Koblenz is the electorate's, where Cliopatria's record of it begins. Bridging entry: the pages opened (Electorate of Trier, Baldwin of Luxembourg) date no acquisition between the Moselle towns; the Baldwin page, covering his archbishopric 1307-1354, names none. The page describes the territory only as 'along the river Moselle between Trier ... and Koblenz'.
1497: the Boppard War. The townsfolk 'turned in 1496 to Maximilian I. This led in 1497 to the Boppard War'; the page does not date its beginning or end within the year.
1497: Boppard 'had to acknowledge the Elector as their ruler'. The year is the page's; the end of the fighting within 1497 is not given.

region.text: the Prüm Abbey lands, incorporated into the electorate in 1576

ledger.note: 1576: Prüm Abbey is incorporated into the Electorate. 'Pope Gregory XIII issued the decree of incorporation, dated 24 August 1574', 'carried into effect in 1576 after the death of Abbot Christopher of Manderscheid' (the Trier electors then served as administrators). The abbot had been a prince of the Empire with a seat on the Ecclesiastical Bench.
1632: French troops capture Trier. 'In 1632 French troops captured the city'; the city had 'opened its gates to Spanish troops' in 1630 against the absolutist Elector Sötern.
1635: Spanish troops retake Trier. 'Spanish troops retook Trier and imprisoned Sötern.' In 1637 Imperial troops dispelled the French garrison of Ehrenbreitstein.
1673: a French army occupies Trier, to 1675. The page gives the span '1673-1675' for the occupation and does not name the war.

1675: the French occupation of Trier ends. Later: captured again in 1684 ('all walls and fortresses were destroyed this time') and 1688, and in 1689 the French 'systematically destroyed' many cities of the electorate; by 1698 Trier had 'only 2,500 inhabitants'. The pages do not date these occupations' ends, so they are not drawn.

1690: the archbishop-electors take up residence at Koblenz. 'The city was the residence of the archbishop-electors of Trier from 1690 to 1801.' The Electorate page has the residence move to Philippsburg Castle at Ehrenbreitstein in the 17th century and the court there 'exclusively' after 1786.
1705: the French stay in Trier, to 1714. The page gives '1705-1714' and, for 1702, an earlier occupation by French troops.
1714: the French occupation of Trier ends (the end of the span '1705-1714' on the page).
1735: French troops occupy Trier again, until 1737.
1737: the French leave Trier ('the French, who stayed until 1737').

ledger.note: 1801: the left bank of the Rhine passes to France. Treaty of Lunéville, 9 February 1801; the 1802 compensation table lists 'Trier: left bank' under France and its client states; Koblenz became capital of the French department of Rhin-et-Moselle (Koblenz page).

region.text: the right bank of the Rhine (Ehrenbreitstein, Montabaur), the 'right bank remnant' of 1803

ledger.note: 25 February 1803: the Final Recess gives the right bank to Nassau. The table of compensation awards lists 'Princes of Nassau' as receiving 'Trier: right bank'; the Electorate page: 'secularized and annexed by Nassau-Weilburg in 1803'. The Imperial Deputation's Final Recess was 'issued at its 46th meeting on 25 February 1803'.

1803: the Electorate of Trier ends. The Final Recess dissolved the ecclesiastical principalities except Mainz, the Teutonic Order and the Order of Malta; the last elector, Clemens Wenceslaus of Saxony, is dated 1768-1803. The Electorate page's infobox also gives 'Treaty of Lunéville: 9 February 1801' as the end date.

wars.name: Four Lords' War
wars.outcome: The Baldwin of Luxembourg page says only that he 'took part in the Four Lords' War against Metz, 1324-1326'; it gives no territorial result.
wars.note: Considered and not drawn: no zone or result on the page. In 1328 Baldwin was captured on the Moselle by troops of Loretta of Sponheim and released after a ransom and unnamed concessions.

wars.name: Boppard War
wars.outcome: The townsfolk turned to Maximilian I in 1496; the war of 1497 ended with Boppard acknowledging the Elector as its ruler.
wars.note: The page dates the war to 1497 only.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War (Trier episodes)
wars.outcome: Trier opened its gates to Spanish troops in 1630, was captured by the French in 1632 and retaken by Spain in 1635, which imprisoned the Elector Sötern; Imperial troops dispelled the French garrison of Ehrenbreitstein in 1637. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The Electorate page narrates these years without naming the war; the occupation of the city 1632-1635 is in the ledger. The Thirty Years' War article was not opened.

wars.name: French occupations of Trier, 1673-1737
wars.outcome: French armies occupied Trier 1673-1675, 1684, 1688, 1702, 1705-1714 and 1735-1737, destroying walls, fortresses and many towns of the electorate in 1684-1689; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page names the wars: the Franco-Dutch War (1673), the War of the Palatinate Succession (1688), the War of the Spanish Succession (1702) and the War of the Polish Succession ('started in 1734; the following year Trier was again occupied'). Only the dated spans 1673-1675, 1705-1714 and 1735-1737 are in the ledger.

zones.text: the electorate's territories on the left bank of the Rhine

wars.outcome: French troops took Trier in August 1794 and occupied the left bank from 1795; the Treaty of Lunéville (9 February 1801) conceded the left bank to France.
wars.note: Rastatt accepted the sacrifice of the left bank on 9 March 1798 and Campo Formio is dated October 1797 on the page.

certainty.note: The electorate was a patchwork of lordships, pledges and exclaves along the Moselle; no survey or treaty line is dated on the pages opened. The circles around Trier and Koblenz (898-1332) are readings, not frontiers.
The Rhine as the line of the French annexation (Lunéville, 9 February 1801); the right bank remnant is still soft.

notes: Six pages opened against a budget of five: the Baldwin of Luxembourg page proved empty of territorial facts. CLIOPATRIA ROW WRONG: all ten shapes (1333..1618, 16,100-17,100 km2) are one misplaced block: about 49 cells in Bavaria (Upper Franconia and the Upper Palatinate, 11.0-12.8 E) and about 21 in the Hunsrück-Nahe country of Rhineland-Palatinate (7.3-8.5 E), none at Trier or Koblenz. The holy-roman-empire-minor-states dossier logs a 1431 'loss' of 25 cells to this row; with the corrected shape that re-cut event is moot. [fx-17, 2026-11-01: that event is now removed from the HRE ledger, and the 25 cells stay in the Empire's shape through the new keyframe holy-roman-empire-minor-states_1431b (1431-1647); nothing changes in this dossier.] The corrected shape (the Moselle valley within 22 km of the river, Trier and Koblenz within 30 km, inside Rhineland-Palatinate, about 8,350 km2) is a reading of the page's 'along the river Moselle between Trier ... and Koblenz'; the right-bank lands (Montabaur, Limburg condominium) are included only through the Koblenz circle; the pages opened date none of their acquisitions. Extent beyond Cliopatria: the dossier runs 898-1803 (the page: 'existed from the end of the 9th to the early 19th century'; 898 imperial immediacy). 898-1332 and 1619-1803 are new keyframes. The date of elevation to an electorate is only a range on the page (infobox 'between 1189 and 1212'; John I, 1189-1212) and is not an event. Not settled: how the Moselle towns between Trier and Koblenz (Wittlich, Cochem, Zell, Bernkastel, Saarburg, Oberwesel) came to the archbishops, and when Montabaur and the Limburg share did; the Electorate page contradicts itself on the move to Koblenz (lead: 'from the 16th century'; body: 'beginning of the 17th century'; 1786 for exclusive residence; the Koblenz page: 1690 to 1801); 1815 (Grand Duchy of the Lower Rhine in Prussia) is outside the state. Counterparts needing dossiers: prum-abbey (imperial abbey, princely from 1222 on its page, to 1576), nassau-weilburg (annexed the right bank in 1803; Cliopatria's Duchy of Nassau begins 1806). Gazetteer names the gazetteer lacks and this dossier uses: Boppard, Prüm, Montabaur (all places); coordinates are the cities' own.
